### Read the Bible: Judges 18, Acts 22, Jeremiah 32, and Psalms 1–2
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/judges-18-acts-22-jeremiah-32-psalms-1-2/
Passage: Judges 18:14-31
Points:
- The Danites seize Micah’s idols and priest to treat them as superstitious talismans for their conquest.
- The opportunistic Levite welcomes a self-serving career promotion rather than offering godly, prophetic guidance.
- Micah unwittingly reveals the utter futility of idolatry by lamenting handmade gods that can be stolen away.
- Raw power and intimidation replace justice as Danite warriors silence Micah and massacre a peaceful people.
- Spiritual apostasy, personal ambition, violence, and superstition inevitably grow together when God's covenant is abandoned.

### Bible Pathways - Mar. 29, 2008
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-mar-29-2008-11571885.html
Passage: Judges 18:24
Points:
- The Danites sought their own interests, robbing Micah's household and bribing his hired priest.
- Micah thought his life was ruined because his supreme devotion rested on handmade deities.
- A person can be completely sincere in religious feelings while remaining fundamentally wrong in practice.
- Anything in life that claims our supreme love and attention ultimately becomes an idol.
- Earthly treasures can easily be taken away, but the living God can never be lost.
